# Shapes where the NATIVE and SELF-HOST compilers allocate materially
# different amounts for the same program.
#
# Format: <case-name> <native-kb> <selfhost-kb> <reason>
#
# TestSelfHostAllocDifferentialX86_64 lists these rather than skipping them,
# following selfhost-wasm-known-divergences.txt: the lane is green with them
# listed, a NEW divergence fails, and a listed shape that comes back WITHIN
# the ratio bound also fails — an allowlist nobody prunes is where bugs go to
# be forgotten.
#
# The KB figures are per-churn growth measured when the entry was written, on
# x86-64. They are reported next to the live numbers on failure, so drift is
# visible without digging through git. They are NOT expected to be stable to
# the byte: they are there to show direction and severity.
#
# Neither compiler is automatically "the wrong one". These entries record a
# disagreement; which side is at fault is decided per entry, and the reason
# says so.

# (empty — the one entry this file carried, with-through-borrowed-param, was
# retired by #6057/#6033: native was leaking the pre-update buffer on every
# `buf = buf.with(i, v)` through a borrowed param because the array cow helper
# decs its own source while the assignment site dec'd again on a rule borrowed
# from the MAP helper. Per-churn growth for that shape is now 0 KB native,
# matching the self-host, so the entry had to go: a listed shape that comes
# back within bound fails this gate by design.)

# A TUPLE carrying an owned pointer, stored into a STRUCT FIELD and rebuilt each
# round. Self-host hands out ~77 B/round that native gives back entirely.
#
# Isolated to the COMBINATION: measured at n=200, a tuple local alone is 0 KB on
# both sides, a struct with a plain array field alone is 0 KB on both sides, and
# only the tuple-inside-a-struct-field shape diverges. So neither the tuple
# reclaim nor the struct-field reclaim is broken on its own — the composed path
# releases something but not everything.
#
# The leak matrix cannot see it. tuple_mixed__structfield__local_store reads
# clean/clean because its cell does not churn: the credit fires and the box comes
# back, which is all a per-round verdict asks. Volume is the half only this gate
# measures, which is why the shape was added here (#7259 tuple wave).
#
# Recorded rather than fixed because the composed path spans two mechanisms
# landed by different sessions — the counted struct-field store and the "TCNT:"
# tier — and guessing at the seam is how the last change in this area became a
# redundant no-op. This entry fails the moment it is fixed, so it cannot rot.
tuple-in-struct-field 0 15 composed tuple-in-struct reclaim releases the box but not all of it; ~77 B/round self-host against 0 native, invisible to the leak matrix
